recipes.name: Braised Flank Steak with Lemon and Garlic

steps.text: Mix flour and garlic powder together in a shallow dish. Season with salt and pepper. Dip steak into the flour mixture evenly coating both sides. Discard remaining flour mixture.

Heat cooking oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Place steak into the skillet and cook until browned, about 5 minutes per side. Stir in chicken broth, lemon juice, garlic, and cloves. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to low. Cover and simmer until steak is tender, about 1 1/2 hours.
To serve, remove steak from the skillet and slice across the grain into thin strips. Place on serving plates and ladle sauce over top.

raw_recipe.headline: Braised Flank Steak with Lemon and Garlic
raw_recipe.description: Braised flank steak becomes flavorful and tender when simmered slowly in chicken broth with garlic, cloves, and lemon juice in an easy stovetop preparation.

review.reviewBody:
Di, this was simply to die for (no pun intended!)I had to use a bit of powdered cloves due to what I had on hand, and I wanted to serve it OVER the buttered egg noodles. There really wasn't quite enough sauce for that. I added 1/2 cup beef broth, and a pckg. of crimimi mushrooms to the pot.
Actually, the meat took more like 2 hours or so to cook... but it was well worth the wait.
Very tender, fall apart and delish over the egg noodles!
Great flavor, but next time I'll make sure to have enough chicken broth in the house!
In any event.... it's a definite addition to the "do again" file.
Thanks!

Delicious and sooooo easy! I used an electric pan by Americraft that cut the simmering time in half. I did add lots of finely chopped garlic and slivered yellow onions. My boyfriend loved it!!!! Thanks for sharing!

As an alternative to braising....try marinating for a few hours and grilling. So so tender and full of flavor. I bought the pack of flap steaks from Costco. line them up in a baking dish to season and marinate. Use black magic seasoning salt, onion powder, garlic powder and olive oil. Turn over with tongs and do the same. Season generously. i let them marinate for 4 hours.....then grill to med or med rare. Totally surprised at how tender and deish they are!!! Seve with corn on the cob, arugula, cranberry and brie salad and twice baked. stuffed!
I doubled up on the cloves, took the meat out after it was browned and sauteed some onions with the garlic before adding the broth and meat back in. Added a bay leaf as well. It was awesome!

I changed the recipe a little bit since I had about a 2lb piece of flank steak. I used the same amount of flour and garlic powder that were suggested for the beef coating, it actually seemed to be a little too much and had plenty of flour leftover to toss. I also sped up the cooking time a bit to about one hour, since I usually don't like to spend more time than that on dinner. I browned both sides of the meat like it said and poured one can of chicken broth, 3 tsp of lemon juice, 2 tsp of minced garlic, sea salt and lots of pepper. I brought the juice to a boil on medium/high heat and covered the pan. I left the meat and steam cook on medium heat for about half hr on one side and then turned meat over for another half hr since broth did not engulf entire meat. After meat cooked, I took it out onto a cutting board to cut into thin slices. I added cornstarch to the juices to thicken and then I added the sliced meat back into the juice/gravy. I boiled a few potatoes and propped open some canned peas as sides. I personally mashed my potatoes with a fork while they were still hot and added the gravy all over them and the meat...it was delicious!

Amazing! 10 minutes of sauteeing, then an hour and a half of hands-free cooking. Who could ask for anything more? I bloomed the garlic and the cloves during the last 1/2 minute of frying the meat. Then I deglazed with the stock. Sauce needed more salt/pepper, and I added 1/2 teaspoon powdered gelatin to the stockstock just before serving, as the flour on the meat didn't add enough viscosity (for my taste). HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

Absolutely delicious! So simple to prepare. I used "Flap Steak", basically the same as flank. The longer you cook, the better. I kept in on low for 2 1/2 hours. For 3 lbs beef, I used two 14oz cans chicken broth, and two heaping tbls of minced garlic. I also added bably mushrooms for last 20 minutes, and served with a good quality egg noodle (DeCecco). My guests raved about this simple dish.

Anyone who did not give this at least 4 stars cannot have made it right. This recipe is amazing. Substituted the cloves with nutmeg and I added a lot more black pepper since I like the spicier flavor. Very good recipe. Also when frying the steak I only left in on for about 30 seconds per side, the recipe asks for 3 mins but there is no need to cook it that much when you are going to braise it for 1 1/2 hours anyway. Just give it some color and keep moving, Made this with chuck steak which is way cheaper and it gave a flavor to the chuck steak that was amazing.

Wow - I must be honest; I am not a huge fan of flank steak, but my family loves it. I have broiled it and grilled it with very good recipes. I was nervous about braising it. I am so glad that I did! I really loved it and so did hubby! I had a 2 pound flank steak so I went heavier on the seasonings. I also added just a little extra broth so the meat was fully covered. It was delicious and so very tender! I added some cornstarch to the liquid to make a gravy as others have suggested - also delicious! I served it with potato pancakes and a broccoli dish. Excellent holiday meal! I will make this again!

I used flap steak. Used vegetable broth since that's what I had on hand with a bit of soy sauce. Simmered for roughly an hour. Came out good and tender. Also used ground cloves, about 1/2 tsp. The gravy thickened up nicely!

My whole family loved this, even the kids. I followed the recipe almost exactly, but also using some unflavored meat tenderizer on the steaks and added sliced mushrooms to the pan (I had blade steaks). The steaks simmered for two hours, then I thickened the liquid with cornstarch, stirred in a bit of sour cream. Served it all over rice, and was very happy with how tender the meat was. No knives needed, it just fell apart and tasted very good. Next time I will try egg noodles instead of rice. Thanks!
I followed some of the suggestions and made a gravy with onions and mushrooms. That added a lot of flavor to what was becoming a pretty boring steak.
Turned out excellent and tender
Excellent! easy, one pan. I added carrots and sliced onion, substituted OJ for lemon juice.

I was looking for a steak braise that didn't use tomatoes, like my mother made when I was a child. Except for using "petite sirloin" instead of the flank steak, I didn't change anything. This was exactly the type of Sunday comfort-food I wanted. Just brown it and let it simmer. I also thickened the braising liquid and made gravy (with mashed potatoes).

I made this today, and was actually really good. My son said to save the recipe and he wants it again soon. The meat was so tender, and the flavors were tasty. The best part of it was that it was a very easy recipe. It's a keeper!
This is a great simple and delicious recipe. Thanks for sharing. We will definitely be making this one again and again.

This was excellent. I followed the directions as listed, but tripled the recipe for my large fam. My only addition was a little cornstarch to thicken up the gravy a bit. Very good & going in our favs.

The meat turned out very tender and flavorful. My picky husband loved it. I've also substituted white wine and beef broth when I didn't have chicken broth. The white wine came out well, but the beef broth did not.
This is the first steak I've made that you only needed a fork to eat!! So tender and juicy. I'll be making it again soon. :)
